newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria pays budgeted 22 bln naira external debt.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria pays budgeted 22 bln naira external debt.

text.p: Nigeria's military government repaid 22 billion naira of its external debt in the six months ended June 30, the same amount as originally budgeted, government accounts published on Thursday showed.
This is $1.0 billion at the rate of exchange of 22 naira to the dollar, which the government uses for official calculations.
In February's delayed budget for the 1996 calendar year the government earmarked $2.0 billion for repayment of external debts.
In his half-year review of the budget finance minister Anthony Ani said Nigeria had not contracted any new foreign loans from the beginning of 1995 until the six months under review.
Nigeria's total foreign debt stood at $32.585 billion at the end of December 1995, compared with $29.429 billion a year earlier. The bulk of the debt -- 66.5 percent -- is owed to the Paris Club.
Ani said teams from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) visited the country five times during the period under review for discussions on the economy.
Nigeria desperately needs to reschedule its growing debt, but has so far not fulfilled necessary conditions for negotiations.
"(Our) Medium Term Economic Strategy (MTES) has now been completed but certain areas need be further discussed with government before it is finalised," Ani said.

"As soon as the issues -- dual exchange rate of the naira currency, decapping of the interest rate, removal of the mandatory sectoral allocation of credit, removal of fertiliser subsidies -- are resolved, the MTES would be finalised and discussions with the Bretton Woods Institutions would commence."
